title: Award Letter Comparison Chart
creator: Beth Kullberg
subject: College Admissions
description: Compare up to four financial aid offers side by side on first-year net price, out-of-pocket cost, projected four-year cost, and debt.

learningObjectives: Students will compare multiple financial aid offers on first-year net price, out-of-pocket cost, projected four-year cost, and total debt, and judge which offers are affordable for their family.

controls: Family yearly contribution and yearly cost increase inputs
Add college, Remove last, and Reset to Marcus buttons
Edit college dropdown and chart buttons (narrow screens)

keyQuestions: Why can a small first-year gap become a large four-year gap?
Why do merit scholarships usually lose value over four years?
What should you ask each aid office before you decide?
commonMisconceptions: The first-year price is the price every year.
An offer that fits in year 1 fits all four years.
assessmentOpportunities: Students compare three offers on four-year net price and borrowing and justify which are affordable for a given family contribution.
